answer: To secure an economy of autonomous agents from Sybil attacks before the dawn of widespread decentralized identity, networks can mandate a computational proof-of-stake bonded to a trusted hardware kernel. Each authorized node must cryptographically sign and whisper its state transitions to the ledger, locking substantial economic collateral. An attacker attempting to flood the system with millions of fake identities faces prohibitive capital expenditure, as every fabricated instance requires an equivalent financial stake and verified execution proof.
